549	/-- The planar bracket is homogeneous in the right argument. -/
550	theorem perp_smul_right (c : ℝ) (a b : Plane) :
551	    perp a (c • b) = c * perp a b := by
552	  simp only [perp, PiLp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]; ring
553	
554	/-- The planar bracket is homogeneous in the left argument. -/
555	theorem perp_smul_left (c : ℝ) (a b : Plane) :
556	    perp (c • a) b = c * perp a b := by
557	  simp only [perp, PiLp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]; ring
558	
559	/-- The planar bracket of a vector with itself vanishes. -/
560	theorem perp_self (a : Plane) : perp a a = 0 := by
561	  simp only [perp]; ring
562	
563	/-- Planar Lagrange identity in coordinates:
564	`(v·w)² + (v×z w)² = |v|² |w|²`. -/
565	theorem lagrange_coord (v w : Plane) :
566	    dot v w ^ 2 + perp v w ^ 2 =
567	      (v 0 ^ 2 + v 1 ^ 2) * (w 0 ^ 2 + w 1 ^ 2) := by
568	  simp only [dot, perp]; ring
569	
570	/-- The squared norm of a planar vector is the sum of its squared
571	coordinates. -/
572	theorem norm_sq_coord (v : Plane) :
573	    ‖v‖ ^ 2 = v 0 ^ 2 + v 1 ^ 2 := by
574	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, Fin.sum_univ_two]
575	  simp [sq_abs]
576	
577	/-- Planar Lagrange identity with norms:
578	`(v·w)² + (v×z w)² = ‖v‖² ‖w‖²`. -/
579	theorem lagrange_norm (v w : Plane) :
580	    dot v w ^ 2 + perp v w ^ 2 = ‖v‖ ^ 2 * ‖w‖ ^ 2 := by
581	  rw [norm_sq_coord, norm_sq_coord, lagrange_coord]
582	
583	/-- Squared norm is differentiable along a differentiable planar curve. -/
584	theorem norm_sq_differentiable {f : ℝ → Plane} (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) :
585	    Differentiable ℝ (fun s => ‖f s‖ ^ 2) := by
586	  have key : (fun s => ‖f s‖ ^ 2) = fun s => (f s 0) ^ 2 + (f s 1) ^ 2 := by
587	    funext s
588	    exact norm_sq_coord (f s)
589	  rw [key]
590	  have h0 : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => f s 0) := fun s =>
591	    (hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf s 0).differentiableAt
592	  have h1 : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => f s 1) := fun s =>
593	    (hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf s 1).differentiableAt
594	  exact (h0.pow 2).add (h1.pow 2)
595	
596	/-- The radial coordinate `t ↦ ‖f t‖` of a differentiable planar curve
597	that never hits the origin is differentiable. -/
598	theorem norm_differentiable_of_ne_zero {f : ℝ → Plane} (hf : Differentiable ℝ f)
599	    (hne : ∀ s, f s ≠ 0) :
600	    Differentiable ℝ (fun s => ‖f s‖) := by
601	  have hs : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => ‖f s‖ ^ 2) := norm_sq_differentiable hf
602	  have key : (fun s => ‖f s‖) = fun s => Real.sqrt (‖f s‖ ^ 2) := by
603	    funext s
604	    rw [Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _)]
605	  rw [key]
606	  intro s
607	  have hpos : ‖f s‖ ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr (hne s))
608	  exact ((hasDerivAt_sqrt hpos).comp s ((hs s).hasDerivAt)).differentiableAt
609	
610	/-- Leibniz rule for the specific angular momentum:
611	`(perp (f) (f'))' = perp (f) (f'')` — the `perp (f') (f')` term
612	drops out by `perp_self`. -/
613	theorem perp_sep_hasDerivAt {f : ℝ → Plane} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) (t : ℝ) :
614	    HasDerivAt (fun s => perp (f s) (deriv f s))
615	      (perp (f t) (deriv (deriv f) t)) t := by
616	  have hf1 : Differentiable ℝ f := hf.differentiable (by norm_num)
617	  have hf2 : Differentiable ℝ (deriv f) := differentiable_deriv_of_contDiff_two hf
618	  have h0 : HasDerivAt (fun s => f s 0) (deriv f t 0) t :=
619	    hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf1 t 0
620	  have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun s => f s 1) (deriv f t 1) t :=
621	    hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf1 t 1
622	  have h0' : HasDerivAt (fun s => deriv f s 0) (deriv (deriv f) t 0) t :=
623	    hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf2 t 0
624	  have h1' : HasDerivAt (fun s => deriv f s 1) (deriv (deriv f) t 1) t :=
625	    hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf2 t 1
626	  have hA : HasDerivAt (fun s => (f s 0) * (deriv f s 1))
627	      (deriv f t 0 * deriv f t 1 + f t 0 * deriv (deriv f) t 1) t :=
628	    h0.mul h1'
629	  have hB : HasDerivAt (fun s => (f s 1) * (deriv f s 0))
630	      (deriv f t 1 * deriv f t 0 + f t 1 * deriv (deriv f) t 0) t :=
631	    h1.mul h0'
632	  have hC := hA.sub hB
633	  rw [show deriv f t 0 * deriv f t 1 + f t 0 * deriv (deriv f) t 1 -
634	        (deriv f t 1 * deriv f t 0 + f t 1 * deriv (deriv f) t 0)
635	      = perp (f t) (deriv (deriv f) t) from by unfold perp; ring] at hC
636	  exact hC

638	/-- Conservation of the specific angular momentum under a central-force
639	acceleration: the torque of a radial acceleration vanishes
640	(`perp a (c • a) = c * perp a a = 0`), so
641	`t ↦ perp (sep t) (deriv sep t)` is constant.  This theorem is the
642	derivable root of the governing-law field
643	`CoulombScatteringData.angular_momentum_law`; the field is kept as the
644	primary contract because its multiplier form `perp = L / m_red` (not
645	merely "constant") is what the conic integration consumes. -/
646	theorem perp_sep_is_const_of_central_force
647	    (sep : ℝ → Plane) (hsmooth : ContDiff ℝ 2 sep) (q : ℝ)
648	    (hnewton : ∀ t : ℝ, deriv (deriv sep) t = q • ((‖sep t‖ ^ 2)⁻¹ • sep t))
649	    (t s : ℝ) :
650	    perp (sep t) (deriv sep t) = perp (sep s) (deriv sep s) := by
651	  have hdiff : Differentiable ℝ (fun τ => perp (sep τ) (deriv sep τ)) := fun τ =>
652	    (perp_sep_hasDerivAt hsmooth τ).differentiableAt
653	  have hzero : ∀ τ : ℝ,
654	      deriv (fun σ => perp (sep σ) (deriv sep σ)) τ = 0 := fun τ => by
655	    rw [(perp_sep_hasDerivAt hsmooth τ).deriv, hnewton τ, smul_smul,
656	      perp_smul_right, perp_self]
657	    ring
658	  exact is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero hdiff hzero t s

```lean
/-- Unit vector at polar angle `θ` in the scattering plane. -/
noncomputable def dirVec (θ : ℝ) : Plane := fun i => if i = 0 then Real.cos θ else Real.sin θ

theorem dirVec_zero (θ : ℝ) : dirVec θ 0 = Real.cos θ := if_pos rfl
theorem dirVec_one (θ : ℝ) : dirVec θ 1 = Real.sin θ := if_neg (by decide)
theorem norm_dirVec (θ : ℝ) : ‖dirVec θ‖ = 1
theorem dot_dirVec (α β : ℝ) : dot (dirVec α) (dirVec β) = Real.cos (β - α)
theorem perp_dirVec (α β : ℝ) : perp (dirVec α) (dirVec β) = Real.sin (β - α)
theorem dot_smul_right (c : ℝ) (a b : Plane) : dot a (c • b) = c * dot a b
theorem dot_smul_left (c : ℝ) (a b : Plane) : dot (c • a) b = c * dot a b
```

593	/-- Coordinate-wise derivative: differentiating a differentiable planar
594	curve and reading off a coordinate equals differentiating the coordinate
595	function. -/
596	theorem hasDerivAt_apply_coord {f : ℝ → Plane} (hf : Differentiable ℝ f)
597	    (t : ℝ) (i : Fin 2) :
598	    HasDerivAt (fun s => f s i) (deriv f t i) t := by
599	  haveI : Fact (1 ≤ (2 : ENNReal)) := ⟨by norm_num⟩
600	  have hg : HasFDerivAt (fun g : Plane => g i)
601	      (PiLp.proj (p := (2 : ENNReal)) (β := fun _ : Fin 2 => ℝ) i) (f t) :=
602	    (PiLp.hasFDerivAt_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) (ι := Fin 2) (E := fun _ => ℝ)
603	      (p := (2 : ENNReal)) (f t) i)
604	  have h1 : HasDerivAt f (deriv f t) t := (hf t).hasDerivAt
605	  have hcomp := hg.comp_hasDerivAt t h1
606	  rw [show (PiLp.proj (p := (2 : ENNReal)) (β := fun _ : Fin 2 => ℝ) i) (deriv f t)
607	      = deriv f t i from rfl] at hcomp
608	  exact hcomp

611	velocity field. -/
612	theorem differentiable_deriv_of_contDiff_two {f : ℝ → Plane}
613	    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) : Differentiable ℝ (deriv f) := by
614	  have h1 : ContDiff ℝ 1 (deriv f) := by
615	    have h := hf
616	    rw [show (2 : WithTop ℕ∞) = 1 + 1 from by norm_num] at h
617	    exact (contDiff_succ_iff_deriv.mp h).2.2
618	  exact h1.differentiable (by norm_num)

622	    perp a (c • b) = c * perp a b := by
623	  simp only [perp, PiLp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]; ring
624

626	theorem perp_smul_left (c : ℝ) (a b : Plane) :
627	    perp (c • a) b = c * perp a b := by
628	  simp only [perp, PiLp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]; ring

634	/-- Planar Lagrange identity in coordinates:
635	`(v·w)² + (v×z w)² = |v|² |w|²`. -/
636	theorem lagrange_coord (v w : Plane) :
637	    dot v w ^ 2 + perp v w ^ 2 =
638	      (v 0 ^ 2 + v 1 ^ 2) * (w 0 ^ 2 + w 1 ^ 2) := by
639	  simp only [dot, perp]; ring
640	
641	/-- The squared norm of a planar vector is the sum of its squared
642	coordinates. -/
643	theorem norm_sq_coord (v : Plane) :
644	    ‖v‖ ^ 2 = v 0 ^ 2 + v 1 ^ 2 := by
645	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, Fin.sum_univ_two]
646	  simp [sq_abs]
647	
648	/-- Planar Lagrange identity with norms:
649	`(v·w)² + (v×z w)² = ‖v‖² ‖w‖²`. -/
650	theorem lagrange_norm (v w : Plane) :
651	    dot v w ^ 2 + perp v w ^ 2 = ‖v‖ ^ 2 * ‖w‖ ^ 2 := by
652	  rw [norm_sq_coord, norm_sq_coord, lagrange_coord]

654	/-- Squared norm is differentiable along a differentiable planar curve. -/
655	theorem norm_sq_differentiable {f : ℝ → Plane} (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) :
656	    Differentiable ℝ (fun s => ‖f s‖ ^ 2) := by
657	  have key : (fun s => ‖f s‖ ^ 2) = fun s => (f s 0) ^ 2 + (f s 1) ^ 2 := by
658	    funext s
659	    exact norm_sq_coord (f s)
660	  rw [key]
661	  have h0 : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => f s 0) := fun s =>
662	    (hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf s 0).differentiableAt
663	  have h1 : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => f s 1) := fun s =>
664	    (hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf s 1).differentiableAt
665	  exact (h0.pow 2).add (h1.pow 2)

668	that never hits the origin is differentiable. -/
669	theorem norm_differentiable_of_ne_zero {f : ℝ → Plane} (hf : Differentiable ℝ f)
670	    (hne : ∀ s, f s ≠ 0) :
671	    Differentiable ℝ (fun s => ‖f s‖) := by
672	  have hs : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => ‖f s‖ ^ 2) := norm_sq_differentiable hf
673	  have key : (fun s => ‖f s‖) = fun s => Real.sqrt (‖f s‖ ^ 2) := by
674	    funext s
675	    rw [Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _)]
676	  rw [key]
677	  intro s
678	  have hpos : ‖f s‖ ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr (hne s))
679	  exact ((hasDerivAt_sqrt hpos).comp s ((hs s).hasDerivAt)).differentiableAt

682	`(perp (f) (f'))' = perp (f) (f'')` — the `perp (f') (f')` term
683	drops out by `perp_self`. -/
684	theorem perp_sep_hasDerivAt {f : ℝ → Plane} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) (t : ℝ) :
685	    HasDerivAt (fun s => perp (f s) (deriv f s))
686	      (perp (f t) (deriv (deriv f) t)) t := by
687	  have hf1 : Differentiable ℝ f := hf.differentiable (by norm_num)
688	  have hf2 : Differentiable ℝ (deriv f) := differentiable_deriv_of_contDiff_two hf
689	  have h0 : HasDerivAt (fun s => f s 0) (deriv f t 0) t :=
690	    hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf1 t 0
691	  have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun s => f s 1) (deriv f t 1) t :=
692	    hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf1 t 1
693	  have h0' : HasDerivAt (fun s => deriv f s 0) (deriv (deriv f) t 0) t :=
694	    hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf2 t 0
695	  have h1' : HasDerivAt (fun s => deriv f s 1) (deriv (deriv f) t 1) t :=
696	    hasDerivAt_apply_coord hf2 t 1
697	  have hA : HasDerivAt (fun s => (f s 0) * (deriv f s 1))
698	      (deriv f t 0 * deriv f t 1 + f t 0 * deriv (deriv f) t 1) t :=
699	    h0.mul h1'
700	  have hB : HasDerivAt (fun s => (f s 1) * (deriv f s 0))
701	      (deriv f t 1 * deriv f t 0 + f t 1 * deriv (deriv f) t 0) t :=
702	    h1.mul h0'
703	  have hC := hA.sub hB
704	  rw [show deriv f t 0 * deriv f t 1 + f t 0 * deriv (deriv f) t 1 -
705	        (deriv f t 1 * deriv f t 0 + f t 1 * deriv (deriv f) t 0)
706	      = perp (f t) (deriv (deriv f) t) from by unfold perp; ring] at hC

/-! #### The unit-direction frame and the polar layer

The Kepler/Binet bridge decomposes into (i) a unit-direction frame
`dirVec` for turning polar-angle statements into vector statements,
(ii) the polar form of angular-momentum conservation
(`perp (sep) (sep') = r² θ'`), which forces the polar angle to be
strictly DECREASING (the clockwise Fig.-1b orbit), and (iii) the Binet
linear ODE for the inverse separation read as a function of the angle.
Steps (i) and the monotone-angle consequences of (ii) are proved here;
the two genuine calculus/ODE leaves are documented `sorry`s with their
derivation routes recorded. -/

/-- The unit vector at polar angle `θ`: `(cos θ, sin θ)`.  The direction
frame for the conic and asymptotic-velocity layers. -/
noncomputable def dirVec (θ : ℝ) : Plane :=
  fun i => if i = 0 then Real.cos θ else Real.sin θ

/-- Zeroth coordinate of the unit-direction frame. -/
theorem dirVec_zero (θ : ℝ) : dirVec θ 0 = Real.cos θ := if_pos rfl

/-- First coordinate of the unit-direction frame. -/
theorem dirVec_one (θ : ℝ) : dirVec θ 1 = Real.sin θ := if_neg (by decide)

/-- `dirVec θ` is a unit vector. -/
theorem norm_dirVec (θ : ℝ) : ‖dirVec θ‖ = 1 := by
  have h : ‖dirVec θ‖ ^ 2 = 1 := by
    rw [norm_sq_coord, dirVec_zero, dirVec_one, Real.cos_sq_add_sin_sq]
  rcases sq_eq_sq.mp (by rw [h]; norm_num : ‖dirVec θ‖ ^ 2 = (1 : ℝ) ^ 2) with h1 | h1
  · exact h1
  · have := norm_nonneg (dirVec θ); linarith

/-- Dot product of two unit-direction vectors is the cosine of the
angle difference. -/
theorem dot_dirVec (α β : ℝ) :
    dot (dirVec α) (dirVec β) = Real.cos (β - α) := by
  simp only [dot, dirVec_zero, dirVec_one]
  rw [Real.cos_sub]; ring

/-- Perpendicular bracket of two unit-direction vectors is the sine of
the angle difference (signed, so orientation-aware). -/
theorem perp_dirVec (α β : ℝ) :
    perp (dirVec α) (dirVec β) = Real.sin (β - α) := by
  simp only [perp, dirVec_zero, dirVec_one]
  rw [Real.sin_sub]; ring

/-- Dot product is homogeneous in the right argument. -/
theorem dot_smul_right (c : ℝ) (a b : Plane) : dot a (c • b) = c * dot a b := by
  simp only [dot, PiLp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]; ring

/-- Dot product is homogeneous in the left argument. -/
theorem dot_smul_left (c : ℝ) (a b : Plane) : dot (c • a) b = c * dot a b := by
  simp only [dot, PiLp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]; ring

namespace CoulombScatteringData

variable {hR : ScalingRegime} (S : CoulombScatteringData hR)

/-- LEAF (polar calculus, Kepler layer): the polar form of the specific
angular momentum, `perp (sep) (sep') = r² θ'`.  Derivation it carries:
differentiate the polar decomposition
`sep = r (cos θ, sin θ)` (`polar_decomposition`) coordinatewise with
`hasDerivAt_apply_coord`, `S.smooth_sep`, `S.smooth_polar_angle`:
`sep' = r' (cos θ, sin θ) + r θ' (-sin θ, cos θ)`; the `perp` bracket
annihilates the radial term (`perp_self` after factoring the radial
vector) and evaluates the tangential term to
`r² θ' (cos² θ + sin² θ) = r² θ'` (`Real.cos_sq_add_sin_sq`).  This is
the calculus identity behind the `r² θ' = const` form of
angular-momentum conservation; the `ContDiff` fields and
`polar_decomposition` are exactly its inputs. -/
theorem angular_momentum_polar (t : ℝ) :
    perp (S.sep t) (deriv S.sep t) = ‖S.sep t‖ ^ 2 * deriv S.polar_angle t := by

theorem polar_angle_deriv (t : ℝ) :
